name: the beach
title: A Grey Beach
description: Wet sand, broken shells, a line of wrack. The wind never quite stops.
Wet sand and broken shells, and a line of wrack. The wind does not stop.
Grey sand, grey sea, a line of wrack. The wind is always here.
_map: position on the route map (grid cells); the camp (travelHours 0) has a path to every place
_arrive: what you see each time you come back: every line whose 'when' holds, in order

text: Back on the sand. The wind finds you at once.
The sand again, and the wind with it.
You come out onto the beach. The wind is waiting.
The beach again: wet sand, a line of wrack.
The beach: the same wet sand, the same wrack.
Wet sand underfoot again. Wrack along the tide line.
The beach in the dark. Only the surf, and a pale line of foam.
In the dark the beach is only sound: the surf, the wind.
Night on the beach. The foam glows faintly at the water's edge.
Smoke rises from the ring of rocks.
A thread of smoke above the ring of rocks.
The fire is still alive in the rocks.
The ring of rocks waits, cold.
The ring of rocks, and cold ash inside it.
No smoke from the rocks. The fire is out.
Shells on the stone under the cliff.
The shells still cling under the cliff.
Under the cliff, the shells wait for the tide.
Fish flash in the shallows.
Something silver turns in the shallows.
The fish are still in the shallows.

explore.name: look around
explore._explore: look around: a pop-up with what you see (view lines whose 'when' holds) and the landmarks not explored yet; no time passes until you pick one

text: Grey sand runs both ways until it bends out of sight. Wrack and broken shells mark the tide line.
The beach stretches both ways, grey and empty. Wrack marks the tide line.
Sand, wrack and broken shells, as far as you can see.

view.text: Behind the dunes, a dark line of trees.
At the far end of the beach, a ring of dark rocks.
At the far end, the ring of rocks, out of the wind.
Past the rocks, a low cliff drops into the surf.
Under the cliff, shells on the wet stone.
The cliff above them is steep. With a rope, it could be climbed.
Beyond the cliff, to the west, the meadows.

nothingLeft: There is nothing here you have not seen.

landmarks.label: the dunes
text: You climb the dunes. From the top the beach runs both ways until it bends out of sight. Behind them the trees begin. A forest, close and hard to miss.
Up the soft sand of the dunes. On the other side, trunks and shade: a forest, close enough to walk to.
From the crest of the dunes you see the island's edge give way to trees. A forest, an hour's walk at most.

landmarks.label: the ring of rocks
text: At the far end of the beach, a ring of rocks breaks the sea wind. It is a natural shelter. You can make a bed here, and build a campfire for warmth.
Rocks stand in a ring, out of the wind. A natural shelter, ready for a bed and a campfire.
The wind cannot reach inside the rock formation. Shelter already made. You can build a bed and a campfire here.

landmarks.label: the low cliff
text: Past the rocks, a low cliff drops into the surf. Shells cling to the wet stone below it. You could pick them and eat them as they are. Cooked, they would go further.
Beyond the rocks, a low cliff meets the sea. Shells crowd the wet stone at its foot. You could eat them raw, or cook them for more.
Under a low cliff past the rocks, shells cover the wet stone. Food, of a kind: raw, or better cooked.

landmarks.label: the shallows
text: In the shallows, a school of small fish turns and flashes. Too quick for bare hands. With a sharp stick you might spear one.
Small fish dart in the shallows, a whole school of them. Your hands are too slow. A spear might do it.
Silver flashes in the shallow water: fish, many of them. Too fast to grab. A sharp stick could reach them.

landmarks.label: climb the cliff
text: You tie the rope around a rock and climb, hand over hand. From the top the land opens out to the west: long grass in waves, bushes, a line of willows. Meadows, an hour's walk away.
With the rope looped round a boulder you haul yourself up, the wind pulling at you. At the top you see what the cliff was hiding: meadows to the west, wide and green, an hour away.
The rope holds. The climb is short but steep. From the top, inland to the west, grass rolls away under the wind: meadows, maybe an hour's walk.
landmarks.requiresText: Too steep to climb without a rope
